meta.scorecard_caveat: Scorecard SAT/ACT percentiles are for enrolled students who submitted scores; at test-optional colleges the range is self-selected high. 244 of 300 colleges in the team file have admit rate + SAT 25/75.
meta.gpa: No published rule is score-only. BigFuture, Scoir, Princeton Review and Appily also compare GPA (BigFuture converts GPA to an SAT-equivalent; method not published on the page read). The Scorecard file has no GPA, so every rulebook below is the SAT-only part of the source's rule.

not_runnable.why: Its tiers are personal-chance bands (reach <15%, target 15-70%, safety >70%) from a chancing model. Only the 10%-admit-rate line and the middle-50% hint are codeable; that is what 'CollegeVine' below encodes.

not_runnable.quote: Reach There is an estimated 5% to 20% chance of admission to the university for the student.
not_runnable.why: Model output, bands are of personal chance (Far Reach 1-5, Reach 5-20, Target 20-75, Likely 75-99). Needs the model.

not_runnable.quote: 3 Reach - Low Chance of Acceptance (11%-25% chance of acceptance)
not_runnable.why: Bands (Wild Card 1-10, Reach 11-25, Maybe 26-60, Likely 61+) are the STUDENT'S chance, not the college's admit rate. The team's script B_backtest_rulebooks.py r_rate applies '30-60 / 60+' to admit rate and says College Essay Guy; the page says neither those numbers nor admit-rate bands. Misattributed.
Need school-level past-applicant data (GPA/test vs outcome); no public thresholds.

rulebooks.name: College Board BigFuture
rulebooks.quote: Reach: Your SAT score, ACT score or estimated GPA is lower than the average score range of last year's first-year class
rulebooks.quote_match: Match: Your SAT score, ACT score or estimated GPA is solidly in the same score range as last year's first-year class.
rulebooks.quote_safety: Safety: Your SAT score, ACT score or estimated GPA is higher than the average score range of last year's first-year class.
rulebooks.rule: if sat < sat25: R; elif sat <= sat75: T; else: L. If sat25 missing: '-'. Admit rate not used.
rulebooks.published_numbers: none on the page read. An older BigFuture text, quoted only on a College Confidential forum post (https://talk.collegeconfidential.com/t/college-boards-misleading-reach-match-safety-categorization/3644455, search snippet, not verified on collegeboard.org), says a score 'within the 25-75 percentiles' is a match.
interpretation_mine: 'solidly in' = inclusive of both ends (not quantified by the source)
rulebooks.gpa: Accepts SAT, ACT or estimated GPA (converted to an SAT score; conversion not published on the page read). Not runnable on GPA here.
rulebooks.test_optional: Not addressed on the page read.
rulebooks.balance: minimum of six colleges: 3 reach, 2 match, 1 safety (same page).

rulebooks.name: The Princeton Review
rulebooks.quote: A dream school is a college where your academic credentials fall in the lower end, or even below, the school's average range
rulebooks.quote_target: A target school is one where your academic credentials ... fall well within the school's average range for the most recently accepted class.
rulebooks.quote_safety: A safety school is one where your academic credentials exceed the school's range for the average first-year student.
rulebooks.rule: lower_end = sat25 + 0.25*(sat75 - sat25); if sat < lower_end: R; elif sat <= sat75: T; else: L.
interpretation_mine: 'lower end' = bottom quarter of that range (0.25 is my number)
'well within' not separated from the upper edge; target runs to sat75
rulebooks.gpa: Credentials = grades, SAT/ACT, class rank; only SAT run here.
rulebooks.balance: 'We recommend starting with 6 schools: 2 dream schools, 2 target schools, 2 safety schools.' Safety list: 'make sure there is at least one school that you know your family can afford.'

rulebooks.name: Scoir (blog wording)
rulebooks.type: named organisation (company blog). Scoir's in-product tiers (Far Reach / Reach / Level / Likely / Very Likely) come from a counselor-set or model 'Acceptance Likelihood', not from this rule: https://help.scoir.com/article/chaajq23y3-the-balanced-list-score
rulebooks.quote: your GPA and/or test scores fall into the lower 25% of what they typically accept for their incoming class
rulebooks.quote_likely: A likely, or safety, school is one where your grades and test scores exceed those of the average admitted student
rulebooks.quote_75th: Typically, having scores above the 75th percentile for a particular school would be considered well above a school's range.
rulebooks.rule: mid = (sat25+sat75)/2; if sat < sat25: R; elif sat > mid: L; else: T.
rulebooks.published_numbers: 'lower 25%' and '75th percentile' appear as words; no admit-rate cut.
interpretation_mine: 'average admitted student' = midpoint of the 25th and 75th (the file has no SAT median)
the 75th-percentile sentence would give a stricter likely line (sat > sat75), which makes Scoir identical to BigFuture
rulebooks.gpa: Blog states likely = GPA above the average admitted GPA.
rulebooks.balance: 'Ideally ... around 3 likely schools, 3-4 level schools, and 2-3 reach schools.'

rulebooks.name: Appily (EducationDynamics)
rulebooks.quote: A reach school is one where your academic profile falls below the 25th percentile of admitted students, or the school has an extremely low acceptance rate
rulebooks.quote_match: typically between the 25th and 75th percentiles. These schools have an acceptance rate around 40-70%
rulebooks.quote_safety: If your numbers fall at or above the 75th percentile, and the school has an acceptance rate of over 70%, it's likely a safety school.
rulebooks.rule: if rate < 0.25: R; elif sat25 missing: '-'; elif sat < sat25: R; elif sat >= sat75 and rate > 0.70: L; else T.
rulebooks.published_numbers: 25th/75th percentiles, 70% (safety), 40-70% (match acceptance rate), 'usually under 25%, sometimes under 10%' (reach).
interpretation_mine: reach admit-rate cut = 25% (the 'usually' figure; the page also says 'sometimes under 10%')
the match '40-70%' is a description, not a gate: a student in the middle 50% at a 30% college stays target
scores above 75th at a college with rate 25-70% = target (safety needs both conditions)
rulebooks.gpa: Profile = GPA, test scores, class rank.
rulebooks.balance: 'Experts typically recommend applying to 7-10 colleges ... about 2-3 reach schools, 3-4 match (target) schools, and 2-3 safety schools.' Financial safety: 'one you can afford even with minimal aid ... at least one college that fits both criteria.'

rulebooks.name: CollegeVine (admit-rate line plus middle 50%)
rulebooks.quote: schools with less than a 10% acceptance rate are reaches for everyone
rulebooks.quote_tiers: Reach ... less than a 15% chance of admission (this is your personal chance, not the school's acceptance rate) ... target ... 15-70% ... Safety ... greater than 70%
rulebooks.quote_scores: Having test scores better than the 75th percentile of students is a good indicator that a college is a safety school.
rulebooks.rule: if rate < 0.10: R; elif sat25 missing: '-'; elif sat < sat25: R; elif sat > sat75: L; else T.
rulebooks.published_numbers: 10% admit-rate line; personal-chance bands 15% / 70% (not codeable without a model); 75th percentile.
interpretation_mine: 'below the averages of accepted students' = below the 25th percentile

no second admit-rate cut: the source says 'unless the school is very selective' but gives no number beyond 10%, so a 1550 student gets 'likely' at a 12%-admit college (an artefact of the literal reading)
rulebooks.gpa: Chancing uses GPA, tests, extracurriculars; blog says grades and scores are 'over a third' of what colleges deem important.
rulebooks.test_optional: Mentions only that test-optional policies changed how scores are used; no rule.
rulebooks.balance: 'A safe bet is to apply to at least 8 colleges ... 2 reach schools, 4 target schools, and 2 safety schools.'

rulebooks.name: Oriel Admissions blog (counselor-blog folk rule)
rulebooks.type: FOLK PRACTICE. The post says 'According to NACAC' and 'Source: NACAC, admissions counselor consensus' with no link; no NACAC document with these numbers was found. Treat as the consultancy's own rule. A second Oriel post (https://orieladmissions.com/how-to-build-a-college-list) uses reach under 10%, target 10-30%, likely above 30%: the same publisher gives two sets of cut-offs.
rulebooks.quote: Any school with an acceptance rate under 15% is a reach for everyone, regardless of your stats.
rulebooks.quote_table: Reach Under 15% Below or at 25th percentile; Match/Target 15-35% Within middle 50%; Likely/Safety 35%+ Above 75th percentile
rulebooks.rule: if rate < 0.15: R; elif sat25 missing: '-'; elif sat <= sat25: R; elif rate >= 0.35 and sat > sat75: L; else T.
interpretation_mine: cells the table leaves empty (in-range student at 35%+ college; above-75th student at 15-35% college) = target
rulebooks.gpa: Mentions GPA and test scores together.
rulebooks.balance: '2-4 reach schools ... 3-5 match/target schools ... 2-3 likely/safety schools.'

BigFuture: SAT/ACT or GPA vs 'average score range' (words)
PrincetonReview: grades, SAT/ACT, class rank vs 'average range' (words)
Scoir: GPA and/or test vs typical accepted (words, some numbers)
'exceed ... average admitted student'; '>75th percentile' = well above (numeric anchor)
Appily: 'at or above the 75th percentile' AND acceptance 'over 70%' (numeric)
reach if 'usually under 25%, and sometimes under 10%' (numeric, hedged)
CollegeVine: personal chance 15-70% (numeric, needs model); middle 50% 'decent indicator' (words)
'less than a 10% acceptance rate are reaches for everyone' (numeric)
notes test-optional changed practice; no rule
OrielBlog: FOLK: claims NACAC, uncited; second post gives 10% / 30%
Cialfo: 'Not Enough Data' when profile is thin
CollegeEssayGuy: named org, personal-chance bands; not an admit-rate rule
